submission.natural_language_explanation: A near token-identity detector for the word ' passionate' (and less so ' passionately') used as a mid-text adjective, in any frame ('is passionate', 'a passionate man', 'The passionate debate'), at 0.6-1.0x max; a few other devotion/care trait words ' compassionate', ' caring', ' loving', ' fervent', ' enthusiastic', ' knowledgeable', ' avid', ' ardent', ' thoughtful' give weak activity (~0.2-0.45x max), while near-synonyms such as ' excited', ' eager', ' devoted', ' dedicated', ' kind', ' warm', ' loyal', ' empathetic', the noun ' passion' and the verb ' cares' stay ~0. Nothing sets a floor: prompts without these words (including punctuation-only text) are silent, and the word is silent as the very first token of a prompt.
